# Embodied Agent Interface

> Embodied Agent Interface (EAI) is an LLM agent benchmark for embodied decision making, introduced in the paper "Embodied Agent Interface: Benchmarking LLMs for Embodied Decision Making" (arXiv 2410.07166), an Oral at the NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track. Authors: Manling Li, Shiyu Zhao, Qineng Wang, Kangrui Wang, Yu Zhou, Sanjana Srivastava, Cem Gokmen, Tony Lee, Li Erran Li, Ruohan Zhang, Weiyu Liu, Percy Liang, Li Fei-Fei, Jiayuan Mao, Jiajun Wu (Stanford University, Northwestern University, Amazon, MIT).

What is Embodied Agent Interface? It is a generalized interface that formalizes embodied decision making tasks and the input-output specifications of LLM-based modules, so that different Large Language Models can be evaluated and compared systematically instead of only by a final task success rate. It unifies a broad set of embodied decision making tasks involving both state and temporally extended goals, four commonly used LLM-based ability modules, and a collection of fine-grained metrics that break evaluation down into error types such as hallucination errors, affordance errors, and various planning errors.

## Key facts

- Four ability modules: Goal Interpretation (grounding natural language instructions to object states, relations, and actions), Subgoal Decomposition (generating a sequence of intermediate states), Action Sequencing (generating executable action trajectories), and Transition Modeling (predicting preconditions and post-effects of operators).
- Evaluation simulators: VirtualHome (V) and BEHAVIOR (B), chosen for task length and scene complexity.
- Dataset scale: VirtualHome has 26 task names and 338 task instructions with 801 annotated goals (340 states, 299 relations, 162 actions); BEHAVIOR has 100 tasks with 673 annotated goals; 438 annotated trajectories in total (average 8.76 steps in VirtualHome, 14.6 in BEHAVIOR); 63 annotated transition models.
- In the VirtualHome subset, 80.7 percent of task categories include instructions with more than 10 action steps.
- Fine-grained error metrics include hallucination errors, affordance errors, and planning errors such as missing steps, wrong order, and extra steps.
- Headline results: o1-preview has the highest action sequencing task success rate (81.0 percent) and execution success rate (91.0 percent) in BEHAVIOR; Mistral Large (73.4 percent) and Gemini 1.5 Pro (73.1 percent) lead in VirtualHome. For subgoal decomposition, o1-preview reaches 89.4 percent in VirtualHome and 57.0 percent in BEHAVIOR. Trajectory feasibility errors are common (41.2 percent). Gemini 1.5 Pro has the highest goal interpretation performance, while Claude-3 Opus excels in goal retrieval rate.
- Unlike evaluations that report only a final success rate, Embodied Agent Interface pinpoints which ability is missing in an LLM and where the problem lies.
- You can evaluate your own model with a single line of code: pip install eai-eval (a Docker image and documentation are also available).
- EAI powers a CVPR 2026 challenge.
